title: ‘Perverse priorities’ made Nikole Hannah-Jones put her cause before her child ore-her-child/
author: Rich Lowry
summary: Rich Lowry argues that Nikole Hannah-Jones favored the interests of Black people with her school choices, but the wrong ones: those of the adults running failing schools rather than the children in them. He describes her experiment as beginning with a savior complex and ending in her daughter falling far behind despite excellent grades. Lowry contends that the officials, principals, and teachers failing New York's students are not white supremacists but largely her political allies, and that portraying school choice as racist keeps her on their side. Citing Brookings research that high-poverty districts spend more per pupil, he rejects funding as the explanation and points to Success Academy's high expectations, discipline, and rigor. He closes by inverting the old line about neoconservatives: the city's schools mugged Hannah-Jones, yet she still will not press charges.
points: Lowry argues most parents with means would immediately remove a child from a school with lunchtime fights, no homework, and ungraded work.
The adults blighting students' futures, he says, largely share Hannah-Jones's politics, and many are African American.
He compares the stance to activists who pushed police to step back, only to see more Black people killed.
Brookings studies show high-poverty, non-white districts spend more per pupil and that spending does not guarantee results.
He contrasts Hannah-Jones with civil rights era parents who integrated schools to obtain a better education for their children.
quotes: New York Times writer Nikole Hannah-Jones thought she was making her educational choices to favor the interests of black people, and she was — just the wrong ones.
What started as a project motivated by a savior complex ended as an episode of educational Munchausen syndrome by proxy.

Most parents who are paying attention and who have the means would immediately get a kid out of a school where there are fights during the lunch period, where there is no homework, where the principal and teachers are routinely absent, and where schoolwork isn’t graded — but Nikole Hannah-Jones persisted.
You can either be with them, and their narrow interest in protecting the school system from serious challenge, or with the kids.

Here, it is supposedly “anti-racist” to keep everyone in disorderly, incompetent public schools — and the victims are black children who have no idea of how little they’ve learned until it’s too late.
The Success Academy charter schools in New York City have shown that disadvantaged kids can thrive when there’s an old-fashioned mix of high expectations, strict discipline and rigorous instruction
New York City’s public schools mugged Nikole Hannah-Jones — and yet she still doesn’t want to press charges.
